quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags work best when used with safety belts and give extra protection in front-end crashes. Wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They are better drivers because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You have your emergency brake on.
You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Always make sure your brake lights work when you drive.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate at a railroad crossing if it is being lowered or raised?

options.text: Yes, as long as an approaching train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.
Yes, if you first look carefully in both directions.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: What can impair a person's ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires being in good physical condition. Alcohol, medications, and drowsiness can all hurt your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: What should drivers do when they see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because they have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is about to appear. Stop unless you are already crossing the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before moving into the other lane, quickly glance over your shoulder to see if any vehicles are in your blind spot.

questions.question: Is smoking or preparing to smoke while driving a distracting activity?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving abilities.
No, it helps keep drivers alert.
Yes, it is a distracting activity.
No, it is not a distracting activity.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a distracting activity.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a dangerous distraction. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: Who has the right-of-way when a funeral procession is present?
questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield the right-of-way to funeral processions. When the lead vehicle enters an intersection, the rest of the procession can follow through, even if the traffic light is red.

questions.question: What will help someone who has had alcoholic drinks feel normal again?
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person recover from alcohol. Nothing else can speed this up.

questions.question: Using your turn signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:

options.text: Is only needed if there is other traffic nearby.
Is good driving and is required by law.
Is only needed during the move, not before.
Is not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is good driving and is required by law.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or turning. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle right or left. Always signal before leaving a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are only found in construction zones.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers stay in the correct lane, show safe passing zones, and warn about upcoming hazards.

questions.question: On long trips, how can you stop yourself from getting sleepy?

options.text: Move your eyes side to side as you drive.

questions.explanation: Stop every few hours on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you are not tired yet.

questions.question: When turning left, you must let these drivers go first:
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists, and any drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when you see:

options.text: A stop sign at an intersection.
A traffic officer telling you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because:

options.text: Drivers go too fast for the conditions.
Drivers check mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers keep a four-second distance between cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers go too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes occur when drivers drive too fast for road conditions. Always follow speed limits and slow down when conditions are bad.

questions.question: To feel less tired on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Keep one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours to rest on long trips. If you get very tired, pull over safely and nap or stay the night.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean stop. Come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: A stop sign has what shape?
questions.explanation: Only stop signs use an octagon shape. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to stop completely before driving on.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on a downhill than smaller vehicles.
Need a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on an uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and heavy. They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles do.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Do not make eye contact. Slow down and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make gestures to show your disapproval.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make eye contact. Slow down and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Slow down and let the aggressive driver pass. Avoid eye contact and do not make gestures. Put distance between your vehicle and theirs.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and back. Never drive next to them and do not follow too closely behind them.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells you to slow down at the intersection ahead. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles or pedestrians go first. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than daytime driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning more difficult, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, use ____ to signal that you are turning.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals fail, use hand signals to tell other drivers which direction you plan to turn.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other traffic is around.
Signal only if you see other traffic.
Signal only in heavy night traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other traffic is around.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you turn, change lanes, or pull away from a curb. Make this a habit every time, not just when other traffic is visible.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles with sirens and flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, what should you know?

options.text: Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. These lines can be horizontal, vertical, or both. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a T intersection is ahead and you should be ready to turn right or left.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving the same way as:
questions.explanation: Lack of sleep and alcohol have the same effects on safe driving. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight impairs your driving as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must you show?
questions.explanation: You must show your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. All three documents are required when driving a vehicle.

questions.question: On a freeway, you missed your turn or exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
Continue driving to the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving to the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. It is illegal to back up on a freeway shoulder.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is:
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. Stop driving if you feel tired.

questions.question: What affects braking distance?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.

questions.explanation: Braking distance is affected by your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: Which substance can impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, prescription medicines, inhalants, and some over-the-counter medicines.
